samira: Hey team — newborn via surrogacy finalized 2026-03-01. How do I add the baby to benefits? The birth certificate lists the surrogate initially and our parentage was established by order on 2026-03-01. Missed open enroll.

olivia (Benefits): Congrats! :tada: Surrogacy/legal parentage can be a QLE. We need the court order of parentage (final decree), the hospital birth record, and either the amended birth certificate showing your names or the court order that directs the registrar to amend the birth cert.

samira: The registrar is slow; amended birth cert may take weeks. We do have the court order (2026-03-01) and hospital birth record. Is that enough to start provisional coverage?

harry (People Ops): Yes — submit Add Dependent in HiBob, choose "Qualified Life Event - adoption/parentage" and upload the court order + hospital record. We'll provisionally enroll pending the amended birth cert. Note: some carriers want the amended cert eventually.

samira: Great. What would be the effective date? Our court order has the parentage effective 2026-03-01 but the child was born 2026-02-25. Which date do carriers use?

olivia (Benefits): Carriers differ. We typically request the coverage effective date to be the court order date (parentage date) when parentage is the event. If you want coverage back to date of birth you'll need carrier approval; we can request retro to 2026-02-25 but approval isn't guaranteed. We'll note requested effective date in the submission.

samira: If it gets approved retro, how will payroll handle deductions? Don't want a huge one-time hit.

devin (Payroll): If Benefits approves a retro start we'll calculate retro premiums. We can usually split the retro charge across up to 2 payroll cycles on request and depending on deadlines. Payroll cycles: 115 and 16end. If docs come in before the 15th cutoff we can aim to include retro in the next pay. Put "split retro" in the HiBob notes and tag @devin.

samira: For international surrogacy there's also a foreign court order and embassy legalization. Any special translation/legalization requirements?

olivia (Benefits): Foreign court orders need certified English translations plus apostille/legalization evidence. An embassy letter confirming recognition helps. Upload all docs to HiBob; we'll accept provisional docs but will need originals or certified copies before final approval.

samira: If the carrier later requires SSN for the dependent, what's the window? Baby won't have SSN at submission.

olivia (Benefits): You have 60 days to provide SSN once issued. If SSN is delayed longer, carrier may require follow-up. We mark records as pending-SSN.

people-ops-bot: Automated: Enrollment change submitted by samira 1911501111 status: pending review. Reference ID: ENR-20260301-5501

samira: Submitted with court order + hospital record, noted "amended birth cert pending" and asked to split retro over two paychecks. Thanks all.

devin (Payroll): Got it  I'll watch the request and flag payroll after Benefits finalizes.

olivia (Benefits): Received. We'll process provisional enrollment and follow up if carriers need the amended birth certificate. Expect an update in 2 business days. Ping this thread if you don't hear back.

samira: Thank you!! :heart:
